issues.description: Raising PerformanceWarning as a hard exception is a category error
issues.detail: PerformanceWarning is a Warning subclass; convention is warnings.warn, not raise. Raising it aborts the write and contradicts both the docstring and the PR description, which openly asks whether an exception is appropriate. The test locks in pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning), cementing the wrong shape. Decide: warn-and-proceed, or rename to a real Error subclass.

issues.description: Unreachable break after raise is dead code
issues.detail: The break statement immediately follows raise PerformanceWarning(msg) inside the loop and can never execute. It signals the author was undecided between fail-fast on first misalignment and aggregating all axes. Pick one policy, document it, and remove the dead statement.

issues.description: safe_chunk_size uses max(1, itemsize) to mask an invariant that should be asserted
issues.detail: np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize) papers over a zero-itemsize case that cannot legitimately occur. Use math.prod for clean int output and assert itemsize >= 1 rather than defending against an impossible state. The interpolated value also risks rendering as np.int64(...) in the user-facing message.

issues.description: Divisibility check inspects only dw[0]; uniform-chunk invariant unstated
issues.detail: The audit examines only the first chunk size per axis, implicitly assuming auto_chunks returns uniform tuples. normalize_chunks can return ragged tails that silently violate alignment. Either check every chunk on the axis or state the invariant in a comment explaining why first-chunk suffices.

issues.description: Operator precedence in `not x % y == 0` is hostile to readers
issues.detail: Python parses this as `not ((x % y) == 0)`, which is what the author wants, but the reader must consult precedence rules. Write `if nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw != 0:` instead. Zero benefit to the current form, real cost to the next maintainer.

issues.description: Test name and assertion semantics disagree with intent
issues.detail: test_zarr_risky_shards_warns asserts pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning, ...) — the name says warns but the test requires an exception. Either rename to ..._raises or, preferably, switch the implementation to warnings.warn and use pytest.warns. Test names are part of the documented intent.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees: the algorithmic idea — use shard shape as previous_chunks so auto_chunks produces shard-aligned chunks — is sound, but the misalignment-detection block is not ready. Two P0 defects dominate: raising PerformanceWarning (a Warning subclass) as a hard exception is a category error that conflates warning and error contracts, and the break after raise is literal dead code revealing an undecided fail-fast-vs-aggregate policy. Secondary concerns: safe_chunk_size leans on max(1, itemsize) instead of asserting the invariant, the divisibility check inspects only dw[0] without stating the uniform-chunk assumption, and `not x % y == 0` is precedence-hostile. Decide warn-or-raise deliberately, name the exception class accordingly, and tighten the loop before merging.
